title: Throttler sticky-session credit serialization bug
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Intermittent incorrect credit accounting observed when requests for the same API key are routed to different edge workers during sticky session handoff. Symptoms are two-fold: (1) some sessions appear to retain a larger-than-allowed remaining credit after a failover (under-throttling), and (2) other sessions see an unexpected immediate debit when the same logical session resumes on the new worker (resulting in double-counts for short-lived requests).

Observed impact: Customers experience bursts of un-throttled traffic lasting ~5-30s followed by catch-up errors and apparent duplicate token charges in billing logs. Affected routes are primarily high-throughput streaming endpoints and some embedding batch endpoints. Incidents correlate with rolling upgrades and ephemeral pod preemption windows.

How we reproduce: 1) Configure a per-key, per-route quota with burst credits and sticky-session affinity. 2) Generate high QPS from a single API key distributed across a small pool of clients (simulate NAT multiplexer). 3) Trigger simulated preemption on the active edge worker (SIGTERM sequence with 10s drain). 4) Observe credit snapshot written to the persistent shard and read by new worker; monitor per-key remaining_credit and meter events in logs.

Hypothesis: The sticky-session snapshot serializer uses an out-of-order flush of in-memory pending-debits during drain. When a handoff writes the snapshot, pending debits that are in-flight are sometimes serialized after the checkpoint marker, causing the accepting worker to replay or reapply those debits. Meanwhile, a lost acknowledgement path allows some workers to skip the pending debits entirely, yielding a transient credit surplus. Root cause likely in the session checkpoint serialization ordering + non-atomic replay path between the edge cache and the central shard.

Immediate mitigation: Add a conservative ephemeral guard that forbids accepting worker from applying any credits until it queries a read-after-write token from the central ledger (temporary strong-read lock per-session). This is a short-term toggle (config flag sticky_strict_handoffs=true) to be rolled to affected clusters only.

Planned fix: Implement atomic handoff protocol: on drain, source worker will write a handoff-record with sequence id and pending-debit batch, then move to draining. Accepting worker must fetch the handoff-record and apply pending-debits exactly-once using seq-id idempotency keys. Additionally, introduce a monotonic per-session sequence number persisted in the shard to avoid replay. Add end-to-end test and chaos test covering preemption/drain windows. Also add metric to track "handoff-sequence-gap" and increment alerting when >0.

Testing: Unit tests for serializer ordering, integration test with two workers and simulated preemption, e2e chaos job in canary environment for 48h.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy read-after-write guard on runtime-1.22 in canary region for 24h. 2) Deploy atomic handoff implementation behind feature flag in canary for 72h. 3) Gradually enable on 10% of production shards, monitor billing diffs, handoff-sequence-gap metric, and error rates for 7 days. 4) Full rollout after no regressions and sign-off from Billing/SRE.
